## Slide 1

- God Vs/Via Science  Chemical Evolution: First Cell
- Ingmar Bitter, PhD

## Slide 2

- Chemical Evolution: First Cell
- How did life start on Earth?
  - What is life?
  - What chemistry is common to all life?
  - Could the common parts arise by chance?
    - How long does it take to make the first cell by chance?
  - Does the common part self assembly honor chemical laws?
  - Is “created by God” a better explanation?

## Slide 3

- Chemical Evolution: First Cell
- What is life?
  - Life self-organizes and self-reproduces.
    - Made of one or more cells with internal stable state
    - Metabolism to make ATP (fuel) and nutrition to grow
    - Some response to stimuli (squeak if poked)
    - Reproduces (DNA replication)

## Slide 4

- Chemical Evolution: First Cell
- What chemistry is common to all life?
  - Life self-organizes and self-(re)produces.
    - Made of one or more cells with internal stable state
    - Metabolism to make ATP (fuel) and nutrition to grow
    - Some response to stimuli (squeak if poked)
    - Reproduces (DNA replication)

## Slide 5

- Chemical Evolution: First Cell
- Could the common parts arise by chance?
  - DNA would need the encoding of all life basics:
    - Cell wall (membrane & pores) and internal structure,
    - Metabolism system (burn food to get ATP, use ATP for work)
    - DNA copy systems
  - Minimal cell & components need  500 proteins
  - DNA needs to encode these proteins
    - Proteins have ~330 amino acids on average
    - 20e330 amino acid combinations per protein
    - 20e330 ^ 500 = 10e214500 combinations for the minimal cell
    - How many tries do we have to make those combinations ?

## Slide 6

- First Cell DNA by Chance ?
- A minimal cell is about 1ym3 in size
- The earth surface area is 510,000,000km2 or ~10e24m2 or 10e36ym2
- So a 1km thick layer around the earth has 10e45ym3
- There is enough space for at most 10e45 minimal cells
- The earth is supposedly life “friendly” for 4billion years
- At 31,556,926 seconds per year we have 10e17 seconds and 10e26 nano seconds
- Thus at most 10e71 chemical reactions trying out DNA combinations could have happened

## Slide 7

- First Cell DNA by Chance ?
- How often can we try to make a minimal cell?
  - 10e71 tries
- What is the expected likelihood of getting it right?
  - 10e71 / 10e214500 = 10e-214429

## Slide 8

- Chemical Evolution: First Cell
- How did life start on Earth?
  - Life self-organizes & self-reproduces (Cells, ATP, DNA)
  - The chemistry common to all life is Cells, ATP, DNA
  - The common parts could not arise by chance in time
  - Does the common part self assembly honor chemical laws?
  - Is “created by God” a better explanation?

## Slide 9

- First Cell by Chance?
- Does the common-part (Cells, ATP, DNA) self-assembly honor chemical laws?
  - Parts of a cell membrane and parts of DNA do self assemble
  - The ATP generator commons to all life is made from multiple proteins and is irreducible complex
  - The DNA read process (needed for protein and enzyme assembly) uses enzymes encoded in the DNA

## Slide 10

- First Cell Self-Assembly?
- Does the first cell self-assembly honor chemical laws?
  - Parts of a cell membrane and parts of DNA do self assemble
  - The ATP generator commons to all life is made from multiple proteins and is irreducible complex
  - The DNA read process (needed for protein and enzyme assembly) uses enzymes encoded in the DNA
    - DNA reading is impossible without them
    - These enzymes cannot self-assemble, but must be build from their DNA recipe
- => First cell self assembly violates chemical laws

## Slide 11

- Chemical Evolution: First Cell
- How did life start on Earth?
  - Life self-organizes & self-reproduces (Cells, ATP, DNA)
  - The chemistry common to all life is Cells, ATP, DNA
  - The common parts could not arise by chance in time
  - First cell self assembly violates chemical laws
  - Is “created by God” a better explanation? … Yes!
    - Logically coherent, documented, believable
    - YES, a better explanation!
